text: 30 Second edition Suspected extrapulmonary TB Table 2 shows the investigations normally used to diagnose the common forms of extrapulmonary TB. In most of these cases, TB will be suspected from the clinical picture and confirmed by histology or other special investigations. Other tests Specialized tests, such as computerized chest tomography and bronchoscopy, are not recommended for the routine diagnosis of TB in children. Some countries use scoring systems for diagnosing TB in children. However, these systems have rarely been evaluated or validated against a “gold standard”; when they have been evaluated, they have performed poorly and variably. They perform particularly poorly in children suspected of pulmonary TB (the most common form) and in children who are also HIV-positive. At this point, therefore, WHO cannot give a recommendation regarding the use of scoring systems to diagnose TB (4). Table 2.
